def: Information missing from a request that the person doing the work needs in order to succeed at it.
deeper: The definition Ambig-SWE uses is deliberately worker-relative: 'missing information that would prevent an expert from being able to create a successful solution.' That rules out two things people conflate with it. A short request is not underspecified if a competent worker could still finish it, and a long request is underspecified if it omits one decision only you can make. The unit of measurement is what the doer still lacks, not how much text you wrote.[^S1]
pitfall: Equating underspecification with brevity, so the fix looks like writing more — which produces long briefs full of detail the agent could have found, while the one decision that broke the run is still missing.
distractor_rationale: Length is the only property of a request that is visible without analysis, so it becomes the proxy for completeness; people who have been told to 'be specific' hear it as 'be lengthy' and add exactly the material that was never in doubt.

def: A choice your request left open that has more than one defensible answer and whose answer exists only in your head.
pitfall: Believing you have none, because every one of them already has an answer in your head and answered questions do not feel like open ones.
distractor_rationale: You experience your own intent as complete — you are reading the request with the answers already loaded — so the blanks are visible to every reader except the one writing.

def: Something your request did not say that the agent can determine by looking at the project itself.
pitfall: Writing these out anyway to be thorough — which costs time, buries the decision blanks in surrounding text, and actively misleads whenever your description of the project is out of date.
distractor_rationale: Listing file paths and current behaviour feels like diligence because it is the part of a brief that is easy to write, so effort flows there rather than to the choices that are hard to articulate.

def: Reading your request as a competent stranger would, with access to your files and none of your history, to expose the decisions you left implicit.
deeper: Anthropic's prompting documentation states it as a rule: 'Show your prompt to a colleague with minimal context on the task and ask them to follow it. If they'd be confused, Claude will be too.' It works because it relocates the request from a head where the blanks are pre-filled to one where they are not. The reliable tell while running it is the word 'obviously' — anything you catch yourself excusing that way is a decision you never stated.[^S4]
pitfall: Running the test while silently supplying context as you read, so the request passes in your imagination and fails with a real reader.
distractor_rationale: Simulating a reader who lacks your knowledge means suppressing knowledge you cannot switch off; the mental version of the test defaults to a colleague who happens to know everything you know.

def: The annotated category for user instructions that omit a detail the task needs, and the largest such category in the study that measured them.
pitfall: Treating missing information as an occasional lapse rather than the normal condition of requests, and so not building a habit that assumes it.
distractor_rationale: People generalize from requests they wrote carefully and remember well, rather than from the ordinary ones, so the base rate feels far lower than the 56.0% the annotation found.

def: The unstated size of a task: whether the request licenses a quick targeted change or a substantial rebuild.
pitfall: Assuming the scale of the work is implied by the scale of the request — a one-line ask is equally consistent with a twenty-minute fix and a two-day restructuring.
distractor_rationale: The effort a task deserves feels self-evident to whoever knows why it is being done, so it reads as context rather than as a decision that has to be transmitted.

def: An explicit statement that a nearby, plausible piece of work is not part of this task.
pitfall: Leaving it unsaid on the grounds that you never asked for the adjacent work — silence about a neighbouring branch is not a decision against it.
distractor_rationale: Not requesting something feels equivalent to excluding it, which holds between people who share the task's history and fails with a reader inferring scope from the words alone.

def: A requirement that output match an existing reference exactly, checkable by comparing the two files.
pitfall: Reaching for it where you do not mean it, then having to relax it mid-run — exact-match requirements are cheap to check and expensive to satisfy when any incidental detail differs.
distractor_rationale: It reads as the strictest available form of 'don't change the output', so it gets applied to cases where you actually meant the visible content to stay the same rather than every byte.

def: A specific choice the agent produced for a decision your request left open, presented in the work with no marker that it was invented.
deeper: The reason it carries no marker is structural. Researchers studying tool-calling agents on imperfect instructions attribute it to the training objective: agents 'tend to arbitrarily generate the missed argument.' Nothing in the process distinguishes a slot filled from your instruction from one filled to keep going, so the output cannot flag the difference — which is why invented values are found by checking the result rather than by reading the report.[^S2]
pitfall: Expecting invented values to look uncertain or hedged in the output, when they appear with exactly the confidence of values you supplied.
distractor_rationale: Human writing signals uncertainty through hedging, so readers scan for hedges as a guess-detector — and find none, because the generation process has no uncertain register to write in.

def: The training objective under which a model produces each next piece of text, leaving no state that corresponds to a value being unknown.
pitfall: Reading a wrong result as a comprehension failure, when the request was understood and the missing slot simply had to be filled with something.
distractor_rationale: 'It misunderstood me' is the familiar explanation from human miscommunication, and it fits the symptom exactly while pointing at a repair — rephrasing — that does not address a gap.

def: An underspecified variant of a standard software benchmark, built to measure whether agents detect missing information, ask about it, and use the answers.
deeper: Its design is what makes the results readable. Complete issues were summarized down to versions with details stripped, so each underspecified case has a paired ground truth — the study can attribute a performance change to the missing information rather than to task difficulty. The authors note this is why they did not use naturally underspecified issues: without a verified complete specification to compare against, an improvement cannot be traced to the gap being closed.[^S1]
pitfall: Quoting its 74% figure as a general expectation, when it is the largest relative gain among the models tested, in a controlled setting where a simulated user always held the answer.
distractor_rationale: A single number travels better than an experimental setting, so the figure gets separated from its three conditions in retelling and arrives sounding like a rate that applies to your own work.

def: A stand-in for the person holding the missing information, used so an agent's clarifying questions can be answered the same way every time.
pitfall: Reading results obtained against one as a forecast for your own runs — the proxy always had the answer, always replied, and never tired of being asked.
distractor_rationale: Controlled conditions are easy to skip past when the finding is about the agent, because the user side reads as neutral apparatus rather than as an assumption doing work in the result.

def: Noticing that a request is missing something — the step that has to happen before any clarifying question can be asked.
pitfall: Assuming an agent that asks good questions when prompted will therefore notice on its own when a request needs them; question quality and gap detection are separate abilities, and the measured weakness is in the second.
distractor_rationale: In people the two abilities travel together — someone who asks sharp questions is someone who spots gaps — so competence at one is read as evidence of the other.

def: Proceeding with a task rather than querying the user, which is what models did by default in the study that tested both.
pitfall: Waiting for the agent to raise a question before you consider a request ambiguous, when silence is the default and carries no information about whether the request was clear.
distractor_rationale: A tool that can ask questions is assumed to ask when it needs to, the way a colleague would, so the absence of questions is read as confirmation that none were needed.

def: Having the agent generate questions about a request before any work starts, and answering them yourself.
deeper: It inverts the direction of effort, and the asymmetry is what makes it pay. Finding your own blanks is hard because they are pre-filled in your head; answering a question about your own intent is easy. Anthropic's documentation packages this as a workflow for larger features, with the agent asking about implementation, edge cases, and tradeoffs until the material is covered, then writing a spec to start from.[^S3]
pitfall: Applying it to every task, when the exchange costs real minutes and a one-line change is finished before the questions are answered.
distractor_rationale: A technique that demonstrably improves results invites uniform application, and the cost side is invisible in any single successful example.

def: A statement about the finished work that can be evaluated true or false without consulting your opinion.
deeper: The two properties Anthropic's guidance names are specific and measurable, and its published pair shows what the second buys: 'Safe outputs' versus 'Less than 0.1% of outputs out of 10,000 trials flagged for toxicity by the content filter.' The good version did not resolve what safety means in principle. It named what evidence would settle the question — a thing to count, a threshold, and the instrument doing the counting.[^S6]
pitfall: Writing one that restates the request in different words, so it is satisfied by any output the agent would have produced anyway.
distractor_rationale: Restating the goal feels like specifying it, and the restatement is genuinely true of the desired result — it just fails to be false of the undesired ones.

def: The property of a criterion that can be settled by observing something, rather than by forming an impression of the work.
pitfall: Confusing a criterion that is precisely worded with one that is checkable — 'handle errors properly' is unambiguous English and still requires your judgment to evaluate.
distractor_rationale: Clarity of phrasing and verifiability feel like the same virtue, so a sentence that reads crisply passes an inspection that was supposed to ask what you would observe.

def: The output, count, timing, or command result an agent returns to substantiate a claim, in place of the claim alone.
pitfall: Accepting a confident restatement of the criterion as evidence of it — 'verified the export completes in 8 seconds' is a verdict from a system that grades itself generously, not a measurement.
distractor_rationale: A specific number inside a sentence reads as measured, so the reported figure is trusted at the same level as a command output would be, despite nothing having been shown.

def: An agent judging the quality or completeness of work it produced itself, which reliably skews positive.
deeper: Anthropic's harness write-up reports the effect on both sides of the arrangement. Agents asked to evaluate their own work respond 'by confidently praising the work — even when, to a human observer, the quality is obviously mediocre'; and an agent assigned to grade another agent, out of the box, would identify real issues and then talk itself into approving anyway. Separation helps, but only once the grader is deliberately tuned toward skepticism.[^S9]
pitfall: Repairing it by asking a sharper question — 'are you sure it's done?' — which routes back through the same generous judgment that produced the first answer.
distractor_rationale: Pressing for confirmation works with people, where a direct challenge prompts a second, more careful look, so it is the natural next move when a report feels thin.

def: An agreement on what done means for a unit of work, settled before any of that work is built.
pitfall: Writing criteria after seeing the output, when your sense of what you wanted has already been reshaped by what you got.
distractor_rationale: Judging finished work feels more grounded than specifying unbuilt work, since there is something concrete in front of you — which is exactly the contamination the ordering exists to prevent.

def: Criteria about how the work went rather than about what is true when it finishes.
pitfall: Accepting 'the script ran without errors' as proof of a migration, when a script that silently skips every row it cannot convert satisfies it completely.
distractor_rationale: An error-free run is genuinely necessary and easy to observe, so it gets promoted from a precondition to the finish line without anyone deciding to make that swap.

def: The verdict for a criterion whose evidence was never returned, distinct from passing and from failing.
pitfall: Collapsing it into a pass because the summary sounded confident, which converts the one honest signal you had into a false clean bill.
distractor_rationale: Two-state grading is the habit everyone brings from tests and checklists, so a criterion with nothing behind it gets sorted into whichever bin the surrounding prose suggests.

def: How an instruction in a brief can be followed — exactly as written, including in the cases you did not intend it to cover.
pitfall: Adding a hedging instruction like 'be conservative' expecting judgment, and getting less output rather than better-judged output.
distractor_rationale: Softening words work as tone-setting between people, who read them as calibration rather than as rules, so they are written into briefs with no expectation that they will bind.

def: An existing artifact you name as the thing to match, so its conventions transfer without being described.
deeper: It is the highest-leverage form of example because the naming is the entire contribution. Which patterns exist in a project is recoverable — the agent can find them. Which one you consider current is not: codebases usually hold several ways of doing the same thing, some of them regretted, and nothing in the files marks which is the good one. Ruling out the bad neighbour matters as much as naming the good one, since an agent inferring from frequency picks the most common rather than the current.[^S3]
pitfall: Pointing at a file you have not opened recently, so the agent faithfully reproduces a convention you abandoned two quarters ago.
distractor_rationale: Your memory of a file is of the version you last worked in, and a reference pattern feels like a fact about the project rather than a claim that needs checking.

def: A word naming a quality rather than a thing or a number: clean, consistent, robust, appropriate.
pitfall: Substituting one adjective for another when a brief is challenged — replacing 'cleaner' with 'well-structured and modern' transfers no more than the original did.
distractor_rationale: Adding qualifying words feels like adding precision, because the sentence gets longer and more considered, while the amount of transferable information stays at zero.

def: A property shared by all your examples that you did not mean to require, and that the agent has no way to distinguish from the one you did.
pitfall: Choosing examples that resemble each other because they are the clearest cases, which teaches their shared incidental features — a length, a prefix, a shape — as requirements.
distractor_rationale: Similar examples feel like a consistent demonstration of one rule, so the set that seems most coherent to the author is exactly the set that transmits the most unintended constraints.

def: A statement that a specific action or class of actions must not occur.
deeper: Its subject has to be a verb. When the subject is a quality — don't be verbose, don't make it generic — the prohibition leaves the whole remaining space open, which is why Anthropic's guidance observes that positive examples of the style you want tend to be more effective than instructions about what to avoid. Actions are bounded by exclusion; qualities are not.[^S4]
pitfall: Using one to specify a quality, so 'don't make it look generic' rules out one output and permits every other non-generic thing the agent might produce.
distractor_rationale: You often know what you dislike more precisely than what you want, so negation feels like the more honest and specific instruction available.

def: The part of a boundary that says why it exists, letting it cover cases the wording never named.
pitfall: Omitting it to keep the brief short, leaving a bare rule that an agent facing an obstacle can reason its way around rather than treat as binding.
distractor_rationale: The reason is obvious to whoever writes the rule, so it reads as padding — and its real function, covering the neighbouring case nobody enumerated, is invisible until a case arrives that the wording missed.

def: Adding steps a request did not ask for, on the agent's own judgment about what the task should include.
pitfall: Treating the additions as harmless because each is an improvement, when the cost lands on your attention: the change you needed to read carefully is now inside a diff too large to read carefully.
distractor_rationale: Extra work looks like generosity rather than risk, and each individual addition survives review on its own merits, so the aggregate cost is never attributed to any one of them.

def: The property of an action that cannot be undone by reverting anything: a deletion, a send, a real charge.
pitfall: Judging reversibility from the repository's point of view, so a shipped API change counts as revertible while the mobile clients parsing the old shape stay broken for months.
distractor_rationale: Version control makes almost everything feel undoable, and the mental model of 'I can roll this back' quietly extends to effects that were never in the repository at all.

def: Whether the change you need to inspect is small enough that you will actually inspect it.
pitfall: Skipping boundaries that protect it because nothing breaks when they are omitted — the damage is a review you performed less carefully, which leaves no trace at the time.
distractor_rationale: Boundaries are learned as a safety tool, so a candidate that prevents no harm looks like a preference rather than one of the few worth its line.

def: The brief section stating what to do with a decision the brief does not cover: ask, or record it visibly and continue.
pitfall: Leaving it out because you believe the other sections are complete, which returns every unforeseen case to the silent guess the rest of the brief was written to prevent.
distractor_rationale: A brief that feels thorough seems to have no residue, so the section handling what is left over reads as redundant right up until something lands in it.

def: One of the four parts of a request in OpenAI's framing: what must stay unchanged, and what the agent should avoid or check with you before doing.
pitfall: Growing the list past the two or three that matter, on the theory that more rules give more control — a long list dilutes the attention available for the ones that count.
distractor_rationale: Each additional rule is individually defensible and costs nothing visible to add, so the list grows monotonically without anyone deciding to make it long.

def: A rewritten request carrying the decisions, finish line, examples, and boundaries that the original left implicit.
pitfall: Treating it as a form to fill in section by section, when its content should be only the decisions that would otherwise be made without you — which differ for every task.
distractor_rationale: A named structure invites completion of every field, and a fully filled template feels more rigorous than a short brief that only carries what was genuinely at risk.

def: A request read as instructions someone must execute, which is what exposes where it runs out.
pitfall: Reading your own request as a description of your intent rather than as instructions, which hides every point where a reader would have to choose.
distractor_rationale: You wrote the words to express what you wanted, so re-reading them replays the intent instead of testing what the text alone supports.

def: A question an agent asks about a specific missing decision before continuing work.
pitfall: Judging the interview by how many questions come back rather than what they ask about — turns spent on file locations the agent could have found are turns not spent on the decisions only you hold.
distractor_rationale: Question count is the one property visible at a glance, and an agent asking a lot of questions looks conscientious regardless of whether any of them needed asking.

def: The setting under which interaction was made mandatory in the study, rather than merely permitted.
pitfall: Writing the interview instruction as an invitation — 'ask if anything is unclear' — which competes with a stronger pull toward being helpful and usually loses.
distractor_rationale: Permission sounds sufficient because a capable assistant would use it, and phrasing it as a requirement feels needlessly heavy-handed for something you assume it wants to do.

def: The named failure where an agent produces a plausible-looking implementation that does not handle the cases you cared about.
pitfall: Letting the surface quality of the output stand in for verification, since well-organized work reads as correct work and the gaps are in the cases nothing exercised.
distractor_rationale: Polish and correctness correlate in human-written work, where care shows in both, so the heuristic is well-earned everywhere except here.

def: A sandboxed mode of an external service used so that trying something does not produce a real-world effect.
pitfall: Leaving it unstated for a task that touches payments, email, or deployment, where the default path is the live one and the effect is not yours to undo.
distractor_rationale: Testing against the real service is often the shortest route to a working result, and nothing in a task description marks which side of that line the agent is standing on.

def: The thing that produces the measurement a criterion is checked against: a command, a query, a diff, a count.
pitfall: Naming a threshold without naming what produces the number, which yields a criterion the agent satisfies with an impression — 'significantly faster' where you wanted a timing.
distractor_rationale: A threshold feels like the hard part of a criterion, so once a number is written the sentence reads finished and the question of who measures it never comes up.

def: A statement about what must remain unchanged when the work is done.
pitfall: Writing criteria only about what should become true, so nothing in the brief protects the behaviour that was already correct.
distractor_rationale: A task is framed as a change, and framing focuses attention on the delta — what stays the same is the background, which is not where anyone looks for requirements.

def: Sending a request cold and letting the run proceed to completion with no questions and no intermediate check.
pitfall: Using it for a task with genuine forks in it, where the cost of a wrong guess exceeds by far the two minutes an interview would have taken.
distractor_rationale: It is faster in every run that happens to go well, and the runs that go well are the ones you remember, since the failures get reframed as bad phrasing.

def: A conversation with no prior context, used so that a request is judged on its own words rather than on what you said earlier.
pitfall: Testing a brief in the session where you developed it, where earlier messages silently supply the very context you were trying to check for.
distractor_rationale: The conversation feels like a workspace rather than an input, so the accumulated exchange is not counted as part of what the agent is reading.

def: A plain text file where a brief is drafted and revised before any of it is sent.
pitfall: Drafting in the chat box instead, which makes revising awkward and pushes you toward sending a first version you would have improved.
distractor_rationale: The prompt field is where requests are made, so it feels like the natural place to compose one — and its shape quietly discourages anything longer than a paragraph.

def: The agent's own account of what it did, which is the weakest available evidence about whether it did it.
pitfall: Grading criteria after reading it, when its framing has already shaped which gaps you are able to notice in the evidence.
distractor_rationale: It is the most readable artifact a run produces and the one placed in front of you, so it is read first by default and everything after is read through it.

def: The set of changes a run produced, read as the record of what actually happened rather than what was reported.
pitfall: Judging its size as a proxy for the work done, when a large one usually means scope was added rather than that more of your task was completed.
distractor_rationale: Volume reads as effort in most kinds of work, so a substantial change looks like a thorough job rather than like a boundary that was missing.

def: Discoverable by the agent from the project itself, without being told.
pitfall: Assuming it means unimportant — recoverable information is often essential to the task, and its property is only that stating it adds nothing.
distractor_rationale: The sorting question is about who supplies a fact, but it gets heard as a question about whether the fact matters, so important-feeling details get written down regardless.

def: Changes confined to what the request named, as opposed to restructuring the surrounding work.
pitfall: Assuming they are the default because they are the smaller option, when an agent applying its own judgment about what a good job includes will often reach for the larger one.
distractor_rationale: Minimal intervention is the professional norm among people, so it reads as the obvious baseline that would only be departed from on request.

def: Fenced or tagged so that examples are visibly examples, not part of the instructions.
pitfall: Pasting examples inline in the flow of a brief, where a demonstration of the style can be read as an instruction to produce that specific thing.
distractor_rationale: In writing for people, an example introduced by 'for example' is unambiguously an example, so the need for a structural marker never arises.

def: The inputs at the boundary of a requirement, where the unstated decisions in a request usually hide.
pitfall: Checking a brief against the ordinary case only, which is the one both you and the agent already agree on, and never against the item that does not fit the pattern.
distractor_rationale: The main case is what the request is about, so it absorbs the attention available for review, while the boundary is where two readings of the same words first diverge.

def: In an example error response, an optional piece of structure that some cases carry and others do not.
pitfall: Including it in every example when you meant it to be conditional, which turns an optional element into a requirement the agent will supply even where there is nothing to put in it.
distractor_rationale: Complete-looking examples feel like better examples, so the temptation is to show every element in each one — exactly the uniformity that creates an unintended rule.

def: A pause where the agent stops and checks with you before taking an action, rather than deciding on its own.
pitfall: Requesting it broadly rather than for the specific actions that warrant it, which produces a stream of prompts you stop reading and therefore protects nothing.
distractor_rationale: More checkpoints feel strictly safer, since each one is an opportunity to catch something, and the way attention degrades across dozens of them is not visible in any single prompt.

def: Named properties written in advance for judging work whose quality is a matter of taste.
deeper: The move is to relocate the taste rather than eliminate it. An Anthropic engineer grading agent-produced frontend work replaced the unanswerable 'is this design beautiful?' with 'does this follow our principles for good design?', backed by four named criteria given to both the agent doing the work and the agent grading it. The judgment did not become objective; it became fixed in advance and transferable, which is what an impression formed after the fact can never be.[^S9]
pitfall: Concluding that a subjective requirement cannot be specified, and falling back to an adjective — when what cannot be scored can still be given named properties fixed before the work.
distractor_rationale: Taste is genuinely not reducible to a number, and that true observation is over-applied into 'therefore it cannot be written down at all', which skips the option in between.

def: A reproduction step written as a concrete sequence, so a criterion tests the reported symptom rather than a proxy for it.
pitfall: Replacing the reproduction with a description of the cause, which lets a confident and wrong explanation of the bug satisfy the criterion while the bug survives.
distractor_rationale: Explaining the root cause feels like deeper evidence than reproducing the symptom, because understanding sounds more rigorous than observation.

def: A term whose meaning has to be defined in the brief, because several defensible definitions produce different results.
pitfall: Using it as though it were self-evident — same name, same size, same content, same record within a time window are all reasonable readings, and the agent picks one.
distractor_rationale: The word feels precise because in any particular situation you have one definition firmly in mind, and the alternatives never surface while you are the only reader.

def: A fact in your own material that stopped being true, and that nothing in the material marks as wrong.
pitfall: Expecting an agent to identify which claims went out of date, when nothing in the files distinguishes a current statement from an obsolete one.
distractor_rationale: Spotting outdated information feels like a comprehension task, and comprehension is exactly what agents are good at — but the knowledge required is about the world outside the files, not about the files.

def: Able to be undone at low cost, which is the property that decides whether an action needs a boundary at all.
pitfall: Spending boundary lines on reversible actions, which crowds out the two or three that protect the things you cannot take back.
distractor_rationale: Every candidate prohibition is individually reasonable, so without an explicit test for which ones earn their place, the list is sorted by how easily each came to mind.

def: Work whose intended scope is small, and which therefore needs its scope stated rather than inferred.
pitfall: Assuming a small request implies a small task, when the same words are equally consistent with a much larger interpretation of what should be delivered.
distractor_rationale: The proportion between request length and work size holds when people brief each other, because a shared sense of proportion fills in — which is precisely what is missing here.

def: A shared destination where an action's effects are visible to other people, and therefore not privately undoable.
pitfall: Judging an action by whether you could reverse it in your own environment, ignoring that anyone reading the shared surface in the meantime has already acted on it.
distractor_rationale: Reversibility is naturally assessed from the agent's working directory outward, and effects that leave that boundary stop being tracked by the same intuition.
